status: Steps 6–11 implemented: explicit source-scoped memory, opt-in personalization and feedback with deterministic repeat suppression.

ownership.tenant: Derived exclusively from the API key.
ownership.registry: Tenant-shared metadata guarded by operation and source grants.
ownership.content: Each record, event, file, run and result belongs to tenant_id + X-User-ID. Schema access does not grant content access.
ownership.received_at: Server UTC time assigned only when an item is first accepted, never supplied by a client.

envelope_semantics.snapshot: record schema; external_id + object_version required; event_id absent; full object payload.
envelope_semantics.upsert: record schema; external_id + object_version + event_id required; full replacement payload, not a partial patch.
envelope_semantics.delete: record schema; external_id + object_version + event_id required; payload must be null.
envelope_semantics.observe: event schema; event_id required; external_id optional; object_version prohibited; object payload. No current-state mutation.
envelope_semantics.versions: Positive integers. Schema versions are explicit and immutable. No implicit latest, coercion, or automatic migration. Record/event version spaces are independent.
envelope_semantics.time: RFC3339 timestamp with offset, normalized to UTC on ingestion. occurred_at is the external fact time; ordering uses object_version, not delivery time.
envelope_semantics.source_sequence: Optional positive integer on changes/observations, unique per tenant+user+collection; stream starts at 1. Snapshots prohibit it. Never inferred from object_version.
envelope_semantics.references: Optional list, at most 20 {collection_id,external_id}; each target must exist and be active under the same owner and an allowed source. observe.external_id additionally links to an active object in the same collection. Semantic external_reference is an external label (e.g. ISBN), not an implicit local link.

pagination.ordering: ascending immutable resource UUID; not a snapshot; concurrent new rows may require restarting enumeration

conventions.filters: Content lists are scoped by collection URL and owner; records support external_id; events additionally support occurred_from (inclusive) and occurred_before (exclusive). Unsupported/repeated query fields return 400.

statuses.400: Malformed DTO, unknown field/query or invalid parameter
statuses.422: Schema, semantic mapping, envelope or payload constraint
statuses.503: Temporary data storage failure; retry identical delivery
statuses.504: Content request exceeded 60 seconds; retry identical deliveries because earlier batch items may have committed.

conventions.rate_limits: Registry and data routes use 120 requests/minute per peer IP per process. RateLimit-* headers; respect RateLimit-Reset. Not a distributed tenant quota.
conventions.compatibility: Existing document/search/query routes retain their request/response bodies. Legacy keys keep legacy:* and catalog:read only. New grants require administrative issuance. Source-restricted keys cannot use unscoped legacy document routes.

batch_ack.atomicity: POST records/events: per-item transactions, at most 100 typed envelopes and 1 MiB. DTO/body failures reject the whole request before writes. Valid DTOs are validated/persisted separately. HTTP 200 alone does not imply every item succeeded.

response.batch_id: UUID for this response, not an idempotency key

batch_ack.retry: Retry failed/unknown items with identical IDs and bodies; duplicate retains original receipt time. 410 is a permanent erasure boundary, never automatically create a new identity. Acknowledgement means committed, not indexed/analyzed.

conventions.idempotency: Registry POST is create-only (409). Ingestion identities: (owner, source, collection, event_id), and (object identity, object_version); a different immutable body conflicts. Time offsets normalize to UTC. JSON key order does not matter. Snapshot and upsert at the same version can share a receipt only when schema, payload, metadata, occurred_at and references agree. A late upsert enriches a snapshot receipt with event identity/sequence. Lower object versions are retained with stale status, without replacing current state. New observations are accepted regardless of occurred_at order.
conventions.schema_migration: Register a new schema version; explicitly transform source payload and send a higher object_version referencing it. Prior versions retain their payload and original schema_version. No automatic reinterpretation or in-place backfill.
conventions.deletion: data:delete permanently erases private payload, metadata, fingerprints and references from current/history rows; retained opaque IDs/versions and erasure fences prevent replay. Referencing records and observation correction chains are erased transitively. DELETE state-event erases its entire object. Collection/source deletes apply only to the current user; registry definitions remain. User delete includes legacy documents/chunks/vectors/knowledge and conversations. Restricted-source keys cannot erase all user data. Existing document writers and query saves are fenced; future workers must recheck fences and evidence versions before commit.
conventions.retention: No automatic expiry: content remains until explicit deletion. Content-free identity markers/fences persist indefinitely; identities are not reusable. Reconnection requires an explicitly new object/collection/source or user identity outside the erased boundary. Source-side queues/backups/provider retention are owned by their operators; this API erases live application content, not external storage.
conventions.imports: Atomic parts (0..100 snapshots, max 1 MiB), 1-based part <=10000, immutable snapshot_id+boundary+completeness. final declares the last part; out-of-order parts are allowed. Identical part replay returns saved acknowledgements. Reconciliation is read-only and paginated; no absent-object deletion. Source must capture a consistent snapshot plus an opaque change-log cursor and continue delivery after that cursor. API stores the boundary but cannot verify an external log.
conventions.completeness: GET coverage reports source_sequence high watermark, missing ranges (at most 100 + truncation flag), unsequenced events, snapshots and erased receipts. GET import status distinguishes declared completeness from all parts received. history_complete is always false; snapshots, contiguous received sequence prefixes and source declarations do not prove complete historical behavior.
conventions.background: Ingestion and its outbox mutation receipt commit in one owner transaction. The PostgreSQL worker/scheduler now consumes this durable intent by fingerprint, commits job plus trigger cursor atomically, and executes with live key/source/fence/lease checks. No result outbox loop. Indexing remains an explicit separate API operation.

future_scopes: memory:read, memory:write, feedback:read, feedback:write are issuable; existing keys gain none implicitly.

schema_subset.name: paiagent-1
schema_subset.root: Non-nullable object; optional $schema with the exact dialect URI.
schema_subset.objects: properties and additionalProperties:false required; required only references declared properties; names match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}.
schema_subset.nullable: type may be [supported_type,"null"] in either order; absent optional fields are not null values.
schema_subset.arrays: Single items schema required; maxItems 1..100 required; minItems optional.
schema_subset.strings: maxLength 1..16384 required; minLength optional. NUL characters and invalid UTF-8 are rejected.
schema_subset.date_time: Calendar-valid RFC3339 timestamp with explicit offset; no leap seconds.
schema_subset.enums: 1..100 scalar values matching type/constraints; enum on object/array is unsupported.
schema_subset.bounds: Finite numeric bounds with absolute value <= 1e308; lower bound cannot exceed upper bound.
schema_subset.annotations: title/description at most 1000 characters each; structural metadata is tenant-shared, not a private content store.
schema_subset.unsupported: All other keywords, including local/remote $ref, are rejected. No coercion, defaults, dynamic code or remote resolution.

mappings.path: JSON Pointer through object properties only, no arrays/wildcards; missing/null means unavailable.

roles.quantity: number/integer, explicit printable unit label of 1..64 characters; use 1 for dimensionless; no conversion
roles.external_reference: string; singleton, does not confer access to another object

capability_contract.selection: Owner and source grants first. Explicit collection/schema version/kind, scalar JSON paths, filters ANDed. current selects current record version; history selects non-erased record snapshots/upserts or independent observations, excluding corrected observations. Snapshots are states, not actions. Unsupported arrays, formulas, code/SQL/tools are rejected.
capability_contract.filters: eq/ne/in use typed non-null scalar values satisfying the pinned field schema. gt/gte/lt/lte are numeric only. is_null matches missing or JSON null; not_null excludes both. All other operators exclude null/missing. in has 1..100 values. Filters/time/metric fields must be selected.
capability_contract.time: Aware half-open [start,end). time_field defaults to delivery occurred_at or a selected date-time path. Null/missing time excluded by periods, otherwise missing_time interval bucket. IANA timezone changes calendar buckets, never timestamp interpretation. Day/week(Monday)/month bucket labels are local start dates, including DST. Comparison periods are non-overlapping and use the same selection/filter.
capability_contract.metrics: count counts received rows; sum/average/min/max require quantity mapping+unit, one selection per metric; no unit conversion. Null/missing quantities skipped. Empty/all-null numeric aggregates null; ungrouped empty count 0. Scalar category grouping preserves types, null/missing share one group. At most 100 groups/buckets per metric/period. Exact input exceeding max_records rejected, never silently sampled. Finite nonzero quantity magnitudes 1e-324..1e308, decimal precision 650 ROUND_HALF_EVEN. Values/differences are decimal strings; average denominator is non-null count. Comparison differences primary-minus-comparison align identical group and absolute calendar bucket; missing group/bucket null, never assumed zero.
capability_contract.retention: Collected successful results (including insufficient_data) persist until explicit erasure/profile deletion. No auto expiry. Inline-only profiles have selections=[]; up to 10 explicit text inputs/500000 total characters; inputs/history/results never written to DB or managed memory automatically; no inline periods or exact metrics. Profiles themselves are persisted, so never put private inline text in profile goals. Responses store=false, no server logs of prompts. Provider operational retention is governed separately by provider/account policy.
capability_contract.budgets: Per-run bounded sources, records, fragments, model calls, input/output token reservations and time. Input reservation conservatively uses UTF-8 bytes + framing including system/schema; output reserves each full max_output_tokens. Capability clients have zero SDK retries. 4MiB selected-source JSON, 8MiB result envelope. search/query rank a bounded sample and always report partial; record projected-field lexical matching, authorized indexed-file cosine with RRF k=60. Other non-summary capabilities use first bounded text batch and disclose partial. Summary processes all selected batches then reduces; budget exhaustion fails explicitly. Durable retries/scheduling require the documented run/trigger APIs; indexing is still explicit. Step10: API synchronous profiles and durable attempts share tenant admission; see background_execution.
capability_contract.freshness: Owner-locked collection outbox signature before/after provider; any collection mutation rejects save 409 input_changed. GET recomputes current/stale, never calls provider. Conservative collection-wide dependencies include absent rows. Erasure purges affected collection results, including correction chains, and cannot race-save them. Scope erasure deletes affected profiles; user erasure deletes all profiles. API-generated run UUIDs now identify durable status metadata in /v1/runs/{run_id}; inline synchronous output remains ephemeral. Internal non-admitted service calls are not public job submissions. Durable jobs use lease/token/live-key fences and atomically commit result plus succeeded state.
capability_contract.minimum_samples: Each selected dataset and each requested period must meet the configured number of received rows; inline uses input count. Otherwise no generation, data_state=insufficient_data; exact metrics still returned. complete_selection describes pinned filtered selection only, never proves full external history.
capability_contract.provider: OpenAI Responses strict JSON schema, store=false, no tools. Incomplete/refused/invalid output and unverified/duplicate source IDs rejected with 502. Failed/time-limited/budget/stale attempts do not overwrite previous success. Schema/source-ID validation does not prove semantic support or causality; real-model evaluation remains separate.

background_execution.worker: python -m app.jobs.worker --concurrency 4 --poll-seconds 1; --once drains currently due work only
background_execution.states: pending -> running -> succeeded|failed|cancelled; retry/expired-lease recovery -> pending with bounded backoff; max_attempts 1..3
background_execution.leases: 90s lease, fresh UUID per attempt. Attempt has whole-execution deadline effective profile seconds+10 (max50). No heartbeat/checkpointer needed within that bounded lease. Expired attempt cannot save. Recovery after process loss waits for lease expiry and applies backoff. Pending work remains in PostgreSQL while web/worker is offline.
background_execution.atomicity: Existing ingestion+outbox receipt transaction is the durable recalculation intent. Scheduler checks full outbox fingerprint and commits coalesced job+trigger cursor together. Result insertion and succeeded run share the owner/lease-checked transaction; unique result.run_id prevents duplicate visible success.
background_execution.triggers: One configuration per owner-private profile, pinned version, captured API-key identity/grant caps. on_change observes mutations after activation baseline; debounce has bounded max_wait. Interval 60..2592000 seconds with optional aware start_at, default now+interval; UTC-duration schedule, no cron inference; missed ticks coalesce, next_due remains anchor-aligned. Result saves create no source outbox. Trigger changes cancel active work and rotate revision; authorization failure disables trigger until reconfigured. TriggerView.enabled is effective state; config.enabled is the submitted setting and may differ after automatic authorization disable.
background_execution.freshness: Input snapshot and data_as_of are recorded at each attempt start, profile version fixed from enqueue. Source changes reject stale save and retry within budget. A trigger can retain one pending successor while a run is active; superseded failed attempt yields to successor. Trigger queue pressure does not advance its dirty signature; changes are retried on later scheduler polls. Opted-in profiles also observe owner memory revision for on-change scheduling; memory source collections are included in job grant/privacy boundaries.
background_execution.authorization: Raw key secret is never stored. Enqueue captures key ID plus scope/source upper bounds. Worker intersects with current live key grants at claim/start/save; revoked/deleted keys or removed source/data/AI grants block processing/persistence. Owner/source/fences always rechecked. Job list/get never expose stored query/history.
background_execution.retention: Async inline is rejected. Collection query/history are persisted in job.input until erasure/profile deletion; no auto-expiry. Old sync inline remains text/output-ephemeral: only run metadata/grants/budget are retained; no content fingerprint is retained; request text/output not saved. Erasure clears job input/fingerprint, cancels attempts, removes dependent results; scoped profile deletion cascades jobs/triggers. Tenant usage keeps content-free reservation totals.
background_execution.quotas: Global short database admission lock serializes queue accounting across worker/API processes. At most 100 active jobs, 2 running jobs and 100 triggers per tenant. Claim order rotates tenants via last_claimed_at; saturated tenants do not block eligible other tenants. Effective profile budget is clamped to server maxima and persisted at admission. UTC daily reservations charge full call/input/output allowances per attempt, including failed/crashed work; no optimistic refunds. Daily quota defers jobs to next UTC midnight; active queue overflow returns429. Cancellation does not refund reservations.
background_execution.polling: GET /runs and GET /results never generate. Job UUID and result UUID are separate; result_id only exists for persisted successful collected output. Idempotency key is owner-scoped, immutable profile+RunInput fingerprint; mode is a delivery preference, not a new computation. Different body conflicts409. Same completed request returns same run/result. Server errors are safe codes only; no prompts/provider/SQL details.

managed_memory.consent: Owner settings.enabled AND immutable profile.personalization.enabled; off by default. Explicit collections, keys/scalar schemas, user-message prefixes and current-field rules. No automatic memory extraction from uploads, conversations, AI answers or run history.
managed_memory.extraction: Deterministic allowlisted scalar JSON fields or exact complete user-message prefix assignments. No arbitrary NLP/code/regex or model calls. Trusted backend declares user-origin fields/messages; attached files/metadata are rejected. Values remain candidates until confirmation. Observations require events, an aware period and sample_count=1 provenance, never an immutable personal trait. Event fields are observations only; preferences require declared user record fields/messages or explicit API writes.
managed_memory.conflicts: One confirmed preference per owner/collection/key. Contradictory candidates cannot overwrite it. Explicit preference PUT is versioned and authoritative. Multiple conflicting assignments in one message remain unpromoted with ambiguous_keys. Delete clears value/provenance and blocks automatic extraction for collection/key; restore=true permits only a new explicit assertion.
managed_memory.context: query/analyze/recommend opt in with memory collections/keys, observations flag, max_items<=20/max_chars<=6000. Only confirmed current-source values with memory:read and current source grants. Feedback separately requires feedback:read. Context is untrusted preference guidance, never factual evidence/source IDs. Read failure falls back via savepoint; no automatic post-answer memory writes. Revision/permissions/versions rechecked before personalized save. Initial optional read has a 1s deadline; feedback collection permissions are batch-checked before use. Period-bound observations must overlap a requested analysis/comparison period when one is supplied.
managed_memory.feedback: Immutable idempotent owner/result request_id; helpful/unhelpful and accepted/rejected/outdated, optional claim_index/all and separate explicit preference. Latest explicit decision per NFKC/casefold/whitespace-normalized proposal text within a profile controls server-side exact repeat suppression. Acceptance is not execution or verified benefit. All repeats withheld -> insufficient_data with reason. Non-recommendation decisions do not suppress output.
managed_memory.profile_scores: Latest feedback record per result/claim target: helpful+accepted minus unhelpful+rejected+outdated; max1000 inspected records and partial flag. Heuristic for caller selection, not confidence or automatic profile replacement.
managed_memory.lifecycle: Normal source updates/corrections invalidate and clear dependent memory; personalized results become stale. Explicit memory/source erasure physically purges dependent results and cancels active personalized jobs. Source/user erasure clears private memory/config/messages and primary fences prevent replay. Owner revision also creates on-change recalculation intent; result saves alone do not change memory or retrigger. Once disabled, further memory/feedback revision changes do not schedule personalization recalculations; disabling itself may request one unpersonalized refresh.
managed_memory.retention: Memory/current explicit messages/feedback persist until deletion; no automatic expiry. Deleted entries keep opaque identity plus collection/key suppression, not value/provenance. Erased message receipts retain identity, not text/fingerprint. Memory-only forget disables use and blocks automatic replay, leaving primary sources/dialogue and separate feedback untouched. Feedback cascades with result; explicit preference supplied through feedback is independent and deleted via memory API. No training/fine-tuning or numeric confidence.
